records.summary: The Vista 10W is WECREAT's lowest-priced enclosed laser: a Class 1 metal enclosure, a lid camera for placing designs and a 16.3 × 11.4 inch work area in a machine 6.5 inches tall, with the air assist pump in the box. At $490 on 2026-11-18 it was priced below the xTool M2 10W ($499) and the Creality Falcon A1 10W ($549) at their makers' stores.
records.fit: First-time laser buyers and crafters who mostly engrave wood, leather, slate and coated tumblers and cut plywood up to about 3 mm, and who want an enclosed machine with a camera for under $500; at 166 mm tall it also fits on a bench beside a 3D printer. Shoppers who cut 6 mm and thicker stock often should step up to the Vision 20W or Vision Pro, and those who want two cameras and add-on color inkjet printing should look at the xTool M2.
caveats: Cutting is slow at 10 W: Tom's Hardware cut 3 mm basswood at 2 mm/s, and a 59-piece plywood job took about 45 minutes; The Gadgeteer said the 10 W head may be too slow for a production shop.
MakeIt!'s time estimates can be far off: Tom's Hardware was quoted 10 minutes 43 seconds for a line engraving that took 41 minutes 36 seconds.

Clear acrylic and bare metal are out: WECREAT lists only "some dark opaque acrylic" as cuttable, and Creative Bloq marked the Vista down for no metal work without the $499 infrared module and for trouble with clear blue materials.

The Gadgeteer found no way to reorder layers front-to-back in MakeIt!, called the crumb tray tricky to fit, and noted the external air-assist pump and the exhaust hose need space beside and behind the machine; a honeycomb panel is a $99 extra.
It must be vented outdoors or filtered: Tom's Hardware reported that smoke and the smell of burning wood filled a garage at once without the optional purifier.
records.question_served: PRIMARY for "best laser engraver for beginners" (lowest price read today for an enclosed Class 1 diode laser with a camera, air assist included) and PRIMARY for "3D printer + laser engraver" as the separate enclosed laser to put beside a printer.

records.summary: The Vision 20W is an enclosed 20 W diode laser whose lid and gantry rise as one to focus on objects up to 140 mm tall, so boxes and tumblers fit without a riser base. The base pack was sold out on 2026-11-18; the Rotary Pack, at $1,390, adds the chuck rotary.
records.fit: Crafters and side-business sellers who engrave tumblers, boxes and other tall items as often as flat sheet and want one enclosed machine with a camera. Shoppers who only engrave flat stock get nearly the same work area from the Vista 10W for $900 less, and those who cut thick wood daily should compare the Vision Pro 45W or an xTool S1 40W ($1,448 list at xtool.com, out of stock there on 2026-11-18).
caveats: Cuts are slow, as with other 20 W diodes: Make: magazine's reviewer said so, and advised venting outdoors because the optional extractor helped but did not remove the fumes.
3DWithUs listed smoke escaping when cutting thicker material and a chuck-only rotary with no roller option, with a dead zone near the chuck.
TechRadar counted the 420 × 290 mm work area and the separately sold fume extractor ($599 today) as its two drawbacks, and noted the full 140 mm height needs the bed taken out.
Tom's Hardware said the external air-assist pump vibrates intensely, called the AI image tool a gimmick, and noticed a strong smell when cutting cast acrylic even with the extractor running.
Clear acrylic and bare metal are out: WECREAT lists only "some dark opaque acrylic" as cuttable with the 20 W diode and sells a separate 2 W infrared head ($499) for engraving metal.
records.question_served: Enclosed laser engraver for tumblers and tall objects without a riser base; the step-up pick for beginners who outgrow 10 W.

records.summary: The Lumos is a 7 kg galvo engraver with a 10 W diode for wood and leather and a 3 W infrared laser for bare metal, a 50 MP positioning camera and a 116 × 116 mm field. At $890 on 2026-11-18 it was priced below the LaserPecker LP4 ($1,039) and the xTool F2 ($1,299) at their makers' stores.
records.fit: Craft-fair sellers and jewelry or gift makers who engrave small metal, wood and leather items on site and want to carry the machine by its handle. Buyers who need to cut sheet material or work larger than a coaster are better served by a gantry machine such as the Vista, and those who want deep metal engraving should look at the Lumos Flex or another fiber laser.
caveats: Tom's Hardware found no shutoff when the cover is raised mid-job and no safety glasses in the box, yet the rotary and slide extension need the cover up; it called the machine suitable for experienced users only.
The 3 W infrared laser engraves metal but cannot cut it, and the galvo beam cuts at a slant toward the edge of the field, which Tom's Hardware warned can spoil tight-fitting parts.
Tom's Hardware had to calibrate the camera, found the material presets limited, and was nagged to buy a premium membership each time the laser connected; most library designs are paid.
The Gadgeteer asked for better written documentation and noted that adding the Lumos over Wi-Fi means typing in its IP address, and that WECREAT warns against lengthening the exhaust hose.
The Essential pack is the bare machine: rotary ($299), slide extension ($399), goggles ($69) and a fume extractor (from $279) are all extra, and it shipped in 3 to 5 business days on 2026-11-18.

records.summary: The Lumos Flex puts a 15 W fiber laser for engraving bare metal and a 15 W diode for wood and leather in one 7.5 kg enclosed galvo unit with a 50 MP camera. At $1,940 on 2026-11-18 it was $489 below the LaserPecker LP5 ($2,429.10) and $609 below the xTool F1 Ultra ($2,549), both 20 W fiber-plus-diode machines.
records.fit: Knife makers, jewelers and gift sellers who need deep or relief engraving on steel, brass and aluminum as well as wood and leather, in a machine they can carry to a booth. Shoppers who only mark coated tumblers and anodized tags can spend $1,050 less on the Lumos, and shops that cut metal or run relief work in volume need a higher-power fiber or MOPA laser.
caveats: Zelpio's reviewer called the software the weakest part: the material library has only a few entries, with no presets for deep brass engraving or relief work.
Relief engraving is slow at 15 W: a detailed piece took eight hours in Zelpio's test, and wood needed a slower speed and a second pass to come out dark.
Metal cutting is limited to foil-thin sheet: WECREAT states 0.3 mm stainless steel and 0.5 mm brass at most.
WECREAT says the Lumos Flex has no phone or tablet app and that LightBurn support depends on the version, and its manual states the rotary is not included.
The work field is 116 × 116 mm; a full wrap on a 40 oz tumbler needs both the Rotary Pro ($299) and the Slide Extension ($399), per the manual.

best laser engraver for beginners.why: At $490 it was the lowest price read today for an enclosed FDA Class 1 diode laser with a positioning camera, and the Basic Pack includes the air assist pump. Work area 16.3 × 11.4 in; LightBurn supported; Tom's Hardware and The Gadgeteer both found setup and MakeIt! easy.
what_rivals_do_better: xTool M2 10W ($499): two cameras and an optional CMYK inkjet module for print-then-cut work.
Creality Falcon A1 10W ($549): deeper bed (305 × 381 mm against about 415 × 290 mm) and LaserGRBL support besides LightBurn.
xTool S1 40W ($1,448 list, out of stock at xtool.com today): four times the diode power and a 23.93 × 15.16 in bed; xTool describes pin-point positioning rather than a camera view.
Glowforge Aura ($999) and Spark ($899): no advantage on price or work area in what was read today; their feature claims were not checked.
WECREAT Vision 20W: twice the power and auto-lift to 140 mm for $900 more.

3D printer + laser engraver.why: As a separate enclosed laser beside a printer the Vista costs $490, stands 166 mm tall, weighs 14.5 kg and vents through its own hose, so printing and lasering can run at the same time. A combo machine read today, the Snapmaker Artisan 3-in-1, starts at $1,799 and swaps toolheads. TechRadar's Vision Pro review remarks that the laser workspace on the Bambu Lab H2D is small next to the Vision Pro's 500 × 320 mm bed.
what_rivals_do_better: A combo machine (Snapmaker Artisan, from $1,799) takes one footprint instead of two.
Creality Falcon A1 10W ($549) is the like-for-like separate enclosed laser from a 3D-printer brand.
xTool M1 Ultra is no longer listed on xtool.com; its successor M2 ($499) adds inkjet printing, not 3D printing.
3D printer + laser engraver.not_verified: Bambu Lab H2D laser combo price could not be read today (store endpoint returned 404).
